rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) before the birth covers the last six weeks before the expected date of delivery. During this time your employer may not employ you unless you expressly declare that you are willing to work. You can withdraw that declaration at any time, with effect for the future.

The six weeks are counted from the expected date of delivery shown in the certificate from your doctor or midwife. With an expected date of 15 November 2026, the period before the birth begins six weeks earlier, in early October 2026. The excerpts do not say which calendar day counts as the first day, so check the exact date with your employer.

If the baby is not born on the expected day, the period before the birth becomes shorter or longer to match. After the birth, your employer may not employ you until eight weeks have passed. This becomes twelve weeks for premature births and multiple births. If the baby comes early, the period after the birth is extended by the time lost before it.

You are expected to tell your employer about the pregnancy and the expected date of delivery as soon as you know. If your employer asks, you are expected to give them a certificate from a doctor or midwife that states that date.

The maternity protection law does not cover self-employed women. They have to arrange their own cover for the time before and after the birth.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
The law sets a limit on back payment rather than an application deadline. Elterngeld (parental allowance) must be applied for in writing. It is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month of life in which the application is received. Months of life before that are not paid. Applications made later lose whole months of payment.

Elterngeld can be drawn from the day of birth. Basiselterngeld can be drawn until the child completes the 14th month of life. Elterngeld Plus can be drawn until the 32nd month of life, as long as at least one parent takes it in consecutive months from the 15th month of life onward.

The same three-month limit applies if you later change the months you chose in your application. A change can apply retroactively only to the last three months of life before the month in which the change request is received. Months already paid out can only be changed in cases of special hardship. One exception: for a month in which Elterngeld Plus was already received, Basiselterngeld can be claimed afterwards.

The Elterngeld office responsible for where you live receives applications and change requests, and it decides on them.

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) is not applied for. You request it from your employer in text form. The statute sets these minimum notice periods before the leave starts:

- Leave before the child's third birthday: at least seven weeks before the start.
- Leave between the third birthday and the eighth birthday: at least 13 weeks before the start.

When you request leave for the period up to the third birthday, you must also state at the same time which periods within two years you will take Elternzeit. If there are urgent reasons, a shorter reasonable notice period is possible as an exception.

If a mother takes Elternzeit directly after the maternity protection period, that period counts toward the two-year period. If she could not request it in time for a reason that was not her fault, she can make the request within one week after that reason ends.

The official family portal explains that text form means a letter without a signature or an email is enough. It also explains that a mother's leave starts only after the maternity protection period, which normally lasts 8 weeks after the birth. So she can give notice after the birth, at least 7 weeks before that period ends. The other parent must give notice 7 weeks before the expected due date if the leave is to start at birth.

Your employer is required to confirm your Elternzeit to you.

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) after the birth normally lasts until eight weeks after delivery. During this time the employer may not employ the mother.

If the baby comes early, two rules can apply.

Born before the expected date. The six weeks before the birth are counted from the expected date of delivery. If the baby arrives earlier, that pre-birth period is shorter. The period after the birth is then extended by the same number of days that the pre-birth period was shortened.

Premature birth. For a premature birth, the period after the birth is extended to twelve weeks. It is also extended by the days by which the pre-birth period was shortened. The statute does not define a premature birth. The federal family portal gives a birth weight under 2,500 grams as one example of a birth that counts medically as premature. It says the total Mutterschutz then rises from 14 to 18 weeks.

The twelve-week period also applies to multiple births. It also applies if a disability in the child is medically confirmed within eight weeks of the birth, but only if the mother applies for it.

One exception: a woman in school or university training may resume that training during the post-birth period if she explicitly asks her place of training. She can withdraw this request at any time.

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
In general, no. Under the Maternity Protection Act, dismissal of a woman is not permitted during her pregnancy, until four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy, and until the end of her protection period after the birth, but at least until four months after the birth. This Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) applies if the employer knows about the pregnancy, miscarriage or birth when giving notice, or is told within two weeks after the dismissal is received. Missing those two weeks does no harm if the delay was not your fault and you inform the employer without delay. The same rules apply to steps the employer takes to prepare a dismissal. The official family portal adds that the protection also applies if you did not yet know you were pregnant, but you must already have been pregnant when you received the dismissal.

There are narrow exceptions. In special cases that are not connected with the pregnancy, a miscarriage or the birth, the highest state authority responsible for occupational safety, or a body it designates, can exceptionally declare a dismissal permissible. Such a dismissal must be in writing and must state the reason. The family portal gives examples such as insolvency, partial closure of the business, a small business that cannot continue without a qualified replacement, or a particularly serious breach of duty. Without the authority's approval, the dismissal is invalid.

If you are dismissed without that approval, the family portal says you must file a claim at the competent labour court to have the dismissal declared invalid. It says the claim must normally be filed within 3 weeks of receiving the written dismissal, and if no claim is filed, the dismissal is treated as valid. You can file it yourself, through a lawyer, or orally at the court's office. The portal also advises contacting the supervisory authority. Challenging the authority's approval is a separate procedure and does not replace the labour court claim.

If you take parental leave after the birth, a separate protection against dismissal under the Parental Allowance and Parental Leave Act can apply from when the leave is requested, with similar exceptions approved by the same type of state authority.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under the federal Elterngeld (parental allowance) law, the entitlement lapses above a set level of zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income).

What the statute says:
- For a single entitled person, there is no entitlement if that person's zu versteuerndes Einkommen in the last completed tax assessment period before the birth was more than 175,000 euros.
- If another person also meets the conditions, for example the other parent, the incomes are added together. The entitlement lapses if the sum of both persons' zu versteuerndes Einkommen is more than 175,000 euros.

Taxable income is not the same as gross income. It is what remains after deductions such as special expenses, insurance contributions, allowances and extraordinary burdens. Gross income is usually clearly higher. The tax office determines the figure, and it appears on the tax assessment notice.

If the tax assessment notice for the last completed year before the birth is not yet available, you can still apply. If the application indicates the limit will probably not be exceeded, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation if the limit later turns out to be exceeded. If it cannot yet be said whether the limit is exceeded, the decision is provisional until proof is provided.

Earlier births: the official guidance page says different, higher limits applied to children born before the current rule took effect. The statutory transitional provision for earlier births is not among the sources I have, so I cannot say which limit applies to a particular birth. The Elterngeld office that handles your application decides whether the limit applies in your case.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
Elterngeld (parental allowance) is counted in monthly amounts for the child's months of life, not calendar months. The law sets these limits.

Basic total. Parents together are entitled to 12 monthly amounts of basic Elterngeld. They get 2 further months, called partner months, if one parent has reduced earned income in two months of the child's life.

Swapping for the longer variant. Instead of one month of basic Elterngeld, a parent can take two months of Elterngeld Plus.

Per-parent limits. One parent can receive at most 12 monthly amounts of basic Elterngeld, plus at most 4 monthly amounts of the partnership bonus. The official family portal explains that each parent can get this bonus as up to 4 extra months of Elterngeld Plus if both work part time at the same time. A parent is only entitled to Elterngeld if they receive it for at least 2 months.

Time windows. Basic Elterngeld can be received until the child completes its 14th month of life. Elterngeld Plus can be received until the child completes its 32nd month, as long as at least one parent takes it in consecutive months from the 15th month onwards.

Premature births. If the child was born at least 6, 8, 12 or 16 weeks before the expected delivery date, the parents' joint total of basic Elterngeld rises to 13, 14, 15 or 16 monthly amounts. The expected date on the doctor's or midwife's certificate is what counts.

These are the general rules. How many months your family actually receives depends on how you split and combine them. That is decided by the Elterngeld authority that handles your application.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) is an extra amount of parental allowance, paid in the longer, lower-monthly variant of parental allowance (Elterngeld Plus in the statute). It is meant for parents who both work part-time at the same time.

What the law says (BEEG §4b):
- Both parents must work no fewer than 24 and no more than 32 hours a week, averaged over the month of the child's life.
- Both parents must also meet the general conditions for parental allowance in §1 of the same law.
- If they do, each parent gets one additional monthly amount for that month.
- Each parent can receive at most four monthly amounts of Partnerschaftsbonus.
- It must be taken for at least two months of the child's life.
- Both parents must take it at the same time, in consecutive months.
- If it later turns out the conditions were not met in every month applied for, the consecutive-months requirement still counts as met.

Single-parent situations (BEEG §4c): one parent alone can receive these additional monthly amounts if they work 24 to 32 hours a week on average in two to four consecutive months, and one of these applies: they meet the conditions for the tax relief amount for single parents and the other parent lives neither with them nor with the child; care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare; or care by the other parent is impossible, for example because of serious illness or severe disability. Economic reasons and being busy with other activities do not count as making care impossible. If one of these situations arises while both parents are already receiving the Partnerschaftsbonus, one parent can continue alone (BEEG §4b(4)).

The official family portal adds that the Partnerschaftsbonus is calculated the same way as the lower-monthly variant, and that if you work outside 24 to 32 hours in a month, the Partnerschaftsbonus for that month must be paid back, for both parents. Months in which the conditions were met are not reclaimed, as long as they were met in at least two months. The portal also says its explanations cover children born after August 2021, and that partly different rules apply to children born before 1 September 2021.

Whether a particular family qualifies, and for how many months, is decided by the responsible parental allowance office.

rows.question: We forgot to apply for Kindergeld. How far back will they pay?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid backdated for at most the six months before the month in which the family benefits office receives your application. Months earlier than that are not paid out, even though the law says the entitlement itself is not affected by this limit. The law does not call this a deadline; it limits how far back payment goes. So each month you wait before applying can mean one more early month that is not paid.

To apply retroactively, state on the application form that you are applying retroactively and from when you want Kindergeld. The application is made in writing or electronically to the family benefits office (part of the Federal Employment Agency). You need your own tax identification number and your child's.

Which months are paid in your case is decided by the family benefits office. Questions about applying can go to the free Federal Employment Agency service line on 0800 4 555530.

rows.question: How much Kindergeld do we get per month for our first child?
rows.reply:

rows.question: How quickly do we have to register the birth at the Standesamt?
rows.reply:
The law says the birth must be reported to the Standesamt (civil registry office) for the place where the child was born within one week (Personenstandsgesetz §18(1)). A government checklist page says "7 working days". The statute says one week, and the statute is what applies.

rows.question: Does my Krankenkasse pay for a midwife?
rows.reply:
Federal law gives women with statutory health insurance a right to midwife care. Under SGB V §24d, an insured woman is entitled to medical care and to help from a Hebamme (midwife) during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth. This includes the examinations to confirm the pregnancy and prenatal check-ups.

After the birth, the right to care from a Hebamme during the postnatal period lasts until twelve weeks after the birth. Care beyond that needs a doctor's order. If the mother cannot care for the child after the birth, the insured child has its own right to the midwife care that relates to the child.

The official family portal says the same thing in plain terms: every woman with statutory health insurance has a right to support from a Hebamme. If you have private health insurance, the portal says to check with your insurer beforehand which services it covers.

Your Krankenkasse (statutory health insurer) decides what it covers in your individual case. Ask it directly if you have questions about a specific service.

rows.question: How do we insure the baby after the birth?
rows.reply:
The law provides Familienversicherung (free family cover for dependants) in statutory health insurance. Children of members of a statutory health insurance fund are insured through that member, provided the child lives or usually stays in Germany. The child must also not be insured in their own right, not be exempt from insurance, not be mainly self-employed, and not have regular monthly income above one seventh of the monthly reference value. Children are covered this way up to their 18th birthday, with longer cover in certain cases.

There is one exclusion that matters for many couples. A child is not covered through Familienversicherung if the other parent, who is married to or in a civil partnership with the member and related to the child, is not a member of a statutory health insurance fund, and that parent's total income regularly exceeds one twelfth of the annual earnings ceiling and is regularly higher than the member's income.

In practice, you need the baby's birth certificate to register the child with the health insurance fund. You must register the birth within 1 week at the registry office responsible for the place of birth, and that office issues the birth certificate. If the baby is born in a hospital or birth centre, the facility notifies the registry office.

Whether your baby qualifies for Familienversicherung is decided by your statutory health insurance fund, not by this service. Questions about private health insurance are outside what we cover. If either parent is privately insured, ask that insurer and the statutory fund directly.

rows.question: When are the first check-ups for the baby?
rows.reply:
The Kinder-Richtlinie (the federal guideline on early detection of illness in children) sets out ten check-ups in the first six years of life. Each one may only be used within its stated period, including the tolerance window. The first four are:

- U1: immediately after birth. It should take place within the first 30 minutes after the baby is born. If no doctor is present at the birth but a midwife is, the midwife should carry it out.
- U2: 3rd to 10th day of life (tolerance: 3rd to 14th day).
- U3: 4th to 5th week of life (tolerance: 3rd to 8th week).
- U4: 3rd to 4th month of life (tolerance: 2nd to 4.5th month).

The same periods also apply to babies born prematurely. Premature birth is taken into account when the doctor assesses the results.

The Gemeinsamer Bundesausschuss (G-BA), which issues the guideline, notes that a decision that entered into force on 20 August 2026 is not yet included in the version it currently offers.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the protection periods before and after the birth, and for the day of birth itself (MuSchG §19, SGB V §24i(3)). These protection periods normally begin 6 weeks before the expected due date and end 8 weeks after the birth.

Who pays it depends on how you are insured:

- If you are a member of a statutory health insurer, you receive Mutterschaftsgeld under the rules of the social code for statutory health insurance (MuSchG §19(1)). For members who are employed when the protection period before the birth begins, it equals the average net daily pay of the last three settled calendar months, up to a maximum of 13 euros per calendar day (SGB V §24i(2)). If the average pay is higher than 13 euros a day, the employer pays the difference as a supplement (MuSchG §20(1)). For other members, it is paid at the level of sick pay (SGB V §24i(2)).
- If you are not a member of a statutory health insurer, Mutterschaftsgeld is paid from federal funds, up to a maximum of 210 euros in total. It is paid on application by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung (MuSchG §19(2)).

On when to apply: the excerpts I have do not set a time limit or deadline for applying. They do say that payment before the birth is based on a certificate from a doctor or midwife stating the expected due date (SGB V §24i(3)). For the timing and procedure of your application, ask your statutory health insurer. If you are not statutorily insured, ask the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung. Whether you qualify and how much you receive is decided by that body.

rows.question: We are not married. Is my partner automatically the legal father?
rows.reply:
No. Under German law, the father of a child is the man who (1) is married to the mother at the time of birth, (2) has acknowledged paternity, or (3) has had his paternity established by a court. If you are not married to each other when the child is born, your partner does not become the legal father automatically.

To become the legal father, he must make a Vaterschaftsanerkennung (acknowledgement of paternity). This is voluntary and requires the mother's consent. It can be made before the child is born.

Both of you must make your declarations in person at a competent office. Examples are the youth welfare office, a registry office, a local court or a notary. That office records his declaration and the mother's consent. Depending on the state, a notary or local court may charge a fee.

An acknowledgement is not effective while another man's paternity exists. For example, this applies if the mother is married to another man at the time of birth. It also cannot be made under a condition or time limit.

If the father does not want to acknowledge paternity, or the mother does not consent, the child, the mother or the presumed biological father can apply to a court to establish paternity.

Being the legal father does not by itself give him parental custody. If you are not married at birth, the mother has custody. Joint custody also requires both parents to declare that they want joint custody, or a court decision. Marrying after the birth also creates joint custody. The youth welfare office advises on custody questions.

rows.question: How do unmarried parents get joint custody?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, if the parents are not married to each other when the child is born, they get joint custody in one of three ways (BGB §1626a(1)):

1. Both parents declare that they want to take on custody together. Each such statement is a Sorgeerklärung (declaration of joint custody).
2. They marry each other.
3. The family court transfers custody to both of them jointly.

If none of these happens, the mother has custody alone (BGB §1626a(3)).

Before any of this, the other parent must be legally recognised as the father. This happens either when he acknowledges the child as his own with the mother's consent, or when a court establishes paternity. Recognising paternity does not by itself give the father custody. A Sorgeerklärung or a court decision is still needed.

A Sorgeerklärung can be made, for example, at the youth welfare office or at a notary. It can also be made before the birth.

The family court route starts with an application by one parent. The court transfers custody, or part of it, to both parents if this does not go against the child's welfare. If the other parent puts forward no reasons against joint custody, and none are otherwise apparent, the law presumes that joint custody does not go against the child's welfare (BGB §1626a(2)). The official family portal adds that the court sets a period for raising such reasons. If none are raised in that period, the court decides in a simplified procedure. In that procedure, the youth welfare office is not heard and the parents are not heard in person.

Your local youth welfare office gives advice on all questions about parental custody.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Frankfurt?
rows.reply:
You apply at the Elterngeldstelle (the state office that decides parental allowance) responsible for where your child lives. Under federal law, each federal state decides which authority handles Elterngeld (parental allowance). The responsible office is the one for the district where the child has their residence in Germany when you first apply. For a child living in Frankfurt, that means the Elterngeldstelle that Hessen has assigned to Frankfurt.

rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
Whether your baby will be German is a decision about your individual case, so we cannot answer it. Here is what the law says in general.

German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) is acquired at birth through a parent when at least one parent holds German citizenship.

A child of foreign parents who is born in Germany acquires German citizenship by birth if one parent meets both of these conditions:
1. has had lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years, and
2. holds an unlimited right of residence (or, for Swiss citizens and their family members, a residence permit under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement).

The law says this acquisition is entered in the birth register where the child's birth is recorded. The office that records the birth there decides whether it applies to your child.

A residence permit is issued to the child automatically if, at the time of birth, both parents (or the parent with sole custody) hold a residence permit, a settlement permit or an EU long-term residence permit. If only one parent holds one, the permit may be issued. If a parent holds a visa or is allowed to stay without a visa, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or visa-free stay ends.

Whether your child also holds Indian citizenship is not covered by these sources. The Indian consular authorities handle that question.

rows.question: We are getting Mutterschaftsgeld. Does that reduce our Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, as a general rule. The law sets out which payments are offset against Elterngeld (parental allowance). Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) under the social insurance rules is offset against Elterngeld. So is the employer's top-up to Mutterschaftsgeld. This applies to payments due for the time from the day of the child's birth.

There is one exception. The one-off Mutterschaftsgeld of at most 210 euros is not offset. The Federal Office for Social Security (Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung) pays it to women who are not members of a statutory health insurer.

The law also says that if these payments cover only part of a month of the child's life, they are offset only against the matching part of that month's Elterngeld.

The official family portal explains the effect for maternity payments for the same child:
- They are offset in full.
- If the maternity payments are higher than the Elterngeld, only the maternity payments are paid for that period.
- If the Elterngeld is higher, the difference is paid as Elterngeld on top.
- Months in which the mother receives these payments for the same child count as months of the basic form of Elterngeld. One day of entitlement in a month is enough for this.

The portal also says the mother's maternity payments are not offset against the father's Elterngeld, only against the mother's.

Different rules apply if the maternity payments are for a different child, for example during a new pregnancy. In that case only part of the Elterngeld is reduced.

How this works out for your family, and how much is paid, is decided by the office that processes your Elterngeld application. These excerpts do not name that office for your area.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, the law allows some work. Working affects how much Elterngeld (parental allowance) is paid, and it brings reporting duties.

The rule in the statute: one condition for Elterngeld is that you do no paid work, or no full-time paid work. You must also live in Germany, live in one household with your child, and care for and raise the child yourself.

How many hours count as full-time is not defined in the statute excerpts available here. The official family portal says you may work part-time while receiving Elterngeld, up to 32 hours a week. That page says its explanation applies to children born after August 2021, and that partly different rules apply to children born before 1 September 2021. Which rule applies to a particular birth is decided by your Elterngeld office.

How work affects the payment: the maximum of 1,800 euros a month applies to full months in which you have no earned income. For months in which you earn less than you did before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as a percentage of the difference between the two incomes. For this calculation, pre-birth income counts up to at most 2,770 euros.

What you must report:
- If you state in your application that you expect to earn income during the payment period, the decision on the amount is provisional. After the payment period ends, you must prove your actual earned income for that time.
- If you state that you expect no earned income, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in case you do have earned income.

The Elterngeld office decides whether you are entitled and how much you receive. It is the place to ask about your own situation.

rows.question: Where and how do we apply for Kindergeld?
rows.reply:
Where to apply: Kindergeld (child benefit) is applied for at the Familienkasse responsible for your area. By law, this is the Familienkasse for the district where the person entitled has their residence. In practice this is usually the Familienkasse of your local Agentur für Arbeit, which normally handles Kindergeld applications. The Familienkasse also makes the decision on the claim.

How to apply: The law says Kindergeld must be applied for in writing. The official portal says you can apply electronically or on paper, using the Familienkasse form. You can fill in the form online, then print and sign it. For a newborn child, you can apply fully online with a valid ELSTER certificate, without printing or signing by hand.

What to include: The application must give your tax identification number and your child's tax identification number. For a child under 18, these numbers are usually all that is needed. If the child was born abroad or lives abroad, include a copy of the foreign birth certificate, or another official document that confirms the birth.

If the Familienkasse asks for more documents, it will give you a date to send them by. If you miss that date, your application can be delayed or refused.

Who applies: Kindergeld is paid to only one person per child. If the child lives in the parents' shared household, the parents decide between themselves who receives it. If they do not decide, the family court decides on application.

Late applications: According to the official portal, Kindergeld can be paid retroactively for up to 6 months. If you apply later, say in the application that you are applying retroactively and from when.

For questions about applying, the Bundesagentur für Arbeit has a free service line: 0800 4 555530.

rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
This product does not cover Bavarian procedures. It covers federal law, Hessen, and the Indian consular track. Elterngeld (parental allowance) itself is federal law, so the rules below apply in Bavaria too. Where to apply and how the Bavarian office handles the paperwork are not covered here. Ask the Elterngeld office responsible for where you live in Bavaria.

Who can claim: a parent who lives or usually stays in Germany, lives with the child in one household, cares for and raises the child, and works not at all or not full time.

How the amount is based: Elterngeld is 67 percent of income from work before the birth. The law counts positive income from employment and also from a trade or business (Gewerbebetrieb) and from self-employed work (selbständige Arbeit), as defined in the income tax law. Taxes and social contributions are deducted, and the income is taken as a monthly average. Where pre-birth income was below 1,000 euros, the percentage rises, up to 100 percent. Where it was above 1,200 euros, the percentage falls, down to 65 percent. For full months with no income from work, the maximum is 1,800 euros a month. The minimum is 300 euros a month, also for people with no income before the birth. If you earn less after the birth than before, Elterngeld is paid on the difference, and pre-birth income counts up to at most 2,770 euros.

Points that matter for self-employed parents: if the tax assessment for the last completed tax period before the birth is not available when you apply, the amount is first decided provisionally, based on the information you credibly provide. The same applies if pre-birth income cannot be determined, or if you expect to have income from work while receiving Elterngeld. If you gave expected income in the application, you must prove your actual income after the payment period ends. If you said you expect no income from work while receiving Elterngeld, it is paid on condition that it can be withdrawn if you do have such income. Payments can also be withdrawn if the tax notice is missing and the income amounts referred to in BEEG §1 (8) turn out to be exceeded. Those amounts are not in the excerpts I have.

The detailed rule on how self-employed profit is worked out is not in the excerpts I have, so I cannot state it. Only the Elterngeld office decides whether you qualify and how much you receive.

rows.question: Can you fill in our Elterngeld application form for us?
rows.reply:
We cannot fill in your Elterngeld (parental allowance) application for you. The form asks for choices and figures about your own family, such as which months you claim and your income. Deciding those for you would be an individual case assessment, which we are not allowed to give. Here is what the law says the application involves.

The application must be made in writing. In it you state for which months of the child's life you claim basic Elterngeld, Elterngeld Plus or the partnership bonus. (BEEG §7)

The person applying signs it. The other entitled parent also signs to confirm they have seen it, except in cases under §4c and where one person has sole custody. At the same time, the other parent can submit their own application. (BEEG §7)

Payment is backdated only for the three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid. (BEEG §7)

The choices in the application can be changed until the end of the payment period. Changes reach back only three months, and are not allowed for months already paid except in cases of particular hardship. One exception: for a month in which Elterngeld Plus was paid, basic Elterngeld can be claimed afterwards. (BEEG §7)

The official family portal lists the documents usually attached: the child's birth certificate and proof of previous income. For employees, this is pay slips for the last 12 months (for mothers, before the month maternity protection begins; for fathers, before the birth). Self-employed people usually attach their last tax assessment. Further documents may be needed depending on the case. (Familienportal FAQ)

Who can help with the form: the authority responsible for your application is the one your federal state designates, in the district where your child lives when you first apply (BEEG §12). Under the same section, these authorities also advise on parental leave. Contact the Elterngeld office for your district in Hessen with questions about filling in the form. It also decides your individual case.

rows.question: Based on our situation, will our Elterngeld application be approved?
rows.reply:
We cannot tell you whether your application will be approved. Only the responsible authority, the Elterngeldstelle, decides an individual case. What we can do is set out the conditions the law attaches.

Under the federal law, a person has a claim to Elterngeld (parental allowance) if they meet all four of these conditions:
1. they have their residence or habitual stay in Germany,
2. they live in one household with their child,
3. they care for and raise this child themselves, and
4. they do not work, or do not work full time.
The law also names some exceptions, for example for people posted abroad who remain subject to German social insurance, and for adoptive parents.

Elterngeld must be applied for in writing. It is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid. The application must state which months you are claiming and in which form.

The official family portal lists the documents usually needed: your child's birth certificate and proof of your previous income. For employees, this means pay slips for the 12 months before maternity protection began (mothers) or before the birth (fathers). Self-employed people usually provide their last tax assessment. Other documents may be needed depending on the case.

The Elterngeldstelle checks these conditions and decides. If you disagree with its decision, the family portal says you can object in writing to the Elterngeldstelle only within one month of receiving the decision.

rows.question: How much tax will we save if I switch to Steuerklasse 3 before the birth?
rows.reply:
We cannot tell you how much tax you would save. That is a calculation for your household, and tax-class choice and its effects belong to a tax adviser or your tax office. We also cannot say how a switch would change any parental allowance you receive.

What the sources say in general:

- Changing your tax class before the birth can change the amount of your taxes and social contributions.
- Parental allowance is calculated from a simplified net income, worked out from your gross income. Income tax is deducted using your tax class, and the factor if you have one. Tax class VI is not used.
- If you changed tax class before the birth, the newest tax class counts for this calculation. The older one is used only if it applied for longer within the whole assessment period than the newer one.
- If you work after the birth, the same tax details are used as for your income before the birth. Changing tax class again after the birth no longer affects your parental allowance.

The parental allowance office decides how your allowance is calculated. Your tax office, or a tax adviser, can answer questions about the tax effect of a switch.
